code: fprintf(outfile, "0x%"PRIx64":\t%s\t\t%s // insn-ID: %u, insn-mnem: %s\n", i->address, i->mnemonic, i->op_str, i->id, cs_insn_name(handle, i->id));
note: The fuzzer-disassembled instruction ID is derived from attacker-controlled input bytes and is later used to query the instruction-name table.

The safety obligation is that the instruction ID must stay within the valid enum range before indexing the name table; otherwise the lookup can return an invalid/NULL result that is later mishandled by the caller path under MSAN.
This table lookup is the target operation that consumes the unchecked instruction ID and produces the instruction-name pointer used by the fuzzer output path.
